results.title: How to 'Force' a Chronological Feed in Facebook's New Design | Lifehacker
results.snippet: You’re probably wondering why I didn’t just wildcard the entire include pattern, or *facebook.com*. Well, doing that means that any other Facebook URL you enter into your browser—like a copied and pasted link to a group, for example—would immediately redirect to the aforementioned “Most Recent” news feed URL. That gets annoying. In this case, we’ve restricted the rule so that only typing facebook.com in your browser sends you to the new URL you want; you can still enter other facebook.com/whatever URLs without issue.

results.title: Facebook Finally Gives Us A Chronological Feed For Friends & Groups
results.snippet: Following sustained demand from users, the Facebook app on Android and iOS has finally restored the chronological feed from friends and Groups. Facebook's 'Home' tab shows an algorithmic feed of 'top stories' rather than a chronological one, frustrating users everywhere.
